summary: Pointe de la Prairie light off Île aux Coudres: a 1931 offshore light on a concrete base, replaced by a 1971-72 pillar light that never had keepers.

light.fog_signal: 1931 light: compressed-air fog horn, 2.5-second blast every 30 seconds; from April 1934, a 3-second blast every 15 seconds (Rochette). Present pillar: no fog signal recorded in the sources read.
light.note: Present light: red and white cylindrical tower, operates year round and 24 hours (Coast Guard list).

structures.type: octagonal concrete base with fog alarm, keepers' quarters and lantern (wedding-cake form)
structures.note: Demolished in 1972 according to Rochette's text.

structures.type: funnel-shaped concrete pillar with circular platform and four-level tower; helicopter pad above the lantern
structures.note: Built 1971 (Quebec record) or 1972 (LighthouseFriends, Le Charlevoisien). Designed by engineer Gérard Laroche; built by Walsh-Canadian Construction Co. Ltd. Height 17 m per LighthouseFriends.

staffing.note: Present pillar automated from construction (Quebec record); keepers at the 1931 light until 1971 (Rochette). No keeper ever assigned to the present tower (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Not open to the public. Visible from the Saint-Joseph-de-la-Rive ferry; best closer view from Chemin des Prairies (tourism listing). LighthouseFriends: grounds and tower closed.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (Coast Guard list; LighthouseFriends). Le Charlevoisien (2012) says Parks Canada owns the lights; see notes_for_editor.

events.note: Construction of the first light begins in June 1930 (Rochette's text).
First offshore light, known as Île aux Coudres Lighthouse, completed July 1931; first keeper J. Pedneault.
Fog signal changed in April 1934 to a 3-second blast every 15 seconds (Rochette's text).
Present pillar tower built (Quebec record). LighthouseFriends and Le Charlevoisien give 1972.
Present pillar automated from construction (Quebec record).
MRC de Charlevoix states its interest in conserving the light, should Parks Canada give it up (Le Charlevoisien).

keepers.note: First keeper of the 1931 light. LighthouseFriends gives 'at least 1937', a documented span, not an end date.

corrections.why: The Quebec heritage record dates construction to 1971; LighthouseFriends and Le Charlevoisien say 1972. The proposed value follows the government record. A human should check it (see notes_for_editor).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rochette's construction dates (June 1930 to July 1931), LighthouseFriends and Le Charlevoisien all agree on 1931 for the first offshore light.

notes_for_editor: 1) Present pillar: 1971 (Quebec heritage record; the Routes des phares listing agrees) against 1972 (LighthouseFriends; Le Charlevoisien). The story gives both. The proposed correction follows the government record. 2) Ownership: the 2012 Le Charlevoisien article says Parks Canada owns the lights; LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns this one; the station record says federal, agency Canadian Coast Guard. Not reconciled. 3) Height and focal height vary by source: 17 m (LighthouseFriends, Routes des phares), 16.4 m (Phares du Saint-Laurent), 14 m tower and 52 m focal plane (tourism listing, not credible against the CCG 15.6 m focal height), 15.6 m focal height (CCG, LighthouseFriends). The story uses the CCG focal height. 4) The 1931 keeper roster is one name (J. Pedneault), from LighthouseFriends only. Rochette's text says keepers stayed until 1971 but names none. 5) Rochette's text is a tourist-guide passage reprinted on a photo site, not checked against the guide itself. 6) The Marine annual reports in the local corpus (to 1923-24) list 'Isle aux Coudres Pole Light' (1901 to 1903) and 'Isle aux Coudres, Wharf Light' (1905): these are island wharf lights, not tied to the point, so they are not used. 7) Le Charlevoisien's line that the light is 'accessible à marée basse' (accessible at low tide) was not used; the site is described as closed. 8) The 1931 construction is not checked against a government document: the Department of Marine annual reports after 1924 are not in the local corpus.
